# Completed per-file measurements replace estimates; a small @test count
# can still hide a large wall cost in background processes and poll loops.
# Actual tested merge (not the standalone PR head):
# The merge and PR head have the same 136 test filenames; the merge includes
# main's terminal-driver changes, including terminal_registry and where tests.
# This was NOT an all-green run. 120 of 136 files have completed, successful
# file_end records (status 0): 109 across the 4 green macOS shards plus 11
# before macOS shard 2 reached the unchanged 30-minute job cap. Only these
# 120 complete measurements are refreshed here (6745s total). In particular,
# all 9 provisional delivery-suite weights now have native macOS timings.
# Never use failed, interrupted, or file_start-only elapsed time as a weight.
# CARRIED ESTIMATES: the remaining 16 files have no completed current-run
# timing. Keep their prior weights from run 36622150859 (2026-09-29, all
# 127 files then completed; see git history), totaling 109s:
# test_self_identity started but was interrupted; its 25s is a prior estimate,
# not a measurement of the current test contents. Refresh these 16 when a
# later run supplies completed successful per-file timings.
# WHY THIS REFRESH: the prior table predicted 1562-1563s per shard, but
# current measurements plus the carried estimates price its actual split at
# 1149/1882/1211/1085/1527s. Updating the weights rebalances those same files
# to 1371/1371/1371/1371/1370s without more jobs, a raised cap, or less coverage.
# These are estimates of file time, not total job time or a promised runtime:
# setup/teardown overhead and runner variance still need native CI validation.
# A file missing from this table is estimated at its average seconds/file,
# never dropped. Coverage does not depend on current weights. The balance
# assertion in tests/test_ci_sharding.bats checks THIS table, not a live run,
# so passing it cannot establish fresh runtime accuracy. Refresh from complete
# status-0 macOS file_end records and explicitly identify any carried values.
# Columns: basename<TAB>seconds. Sorted by basename for a legible diff.
